sections.title: Form and range
sections.text: The catalogue spelling “Melocactus lemarii” appears to be a typo; the taxonomic references consulted give Melocactus lemairei. This species of the eastern Caribbean, including Hispaniola, grows on dry plains and rocky ground. Reliable dimensions were not established by the botanical sources consulted.

sections.title: Cephalium and flowering
sections.text: The solitary cactus is globose to shortly cylindrical and develops a woolly, reddish apical cephalium at maturity. Small pink flowers emerge from the cephalium, followed by red fruits.

sections.title: Edibility
sections.text: No reliable food use was found for this species.
